The '''2026 season''' is the eleventh  season for [[Islamabad United]] in the [[Pakistan Super League]] (PSL) for men's cricket. After renewing their franchise rights for the 2026–2035 cycle, the three-time champions enter the season under new leadership and a revamped recruitment model, as the league transitioned from a draft to a player auction.<ref name="PCBRetention">{{cite press release |title=Six teams announce player retentions for HBL PSL 2026 |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/six-teams-announce-player-retentions-for-hbl-psl-2026-.html |publisher=[[Pakistan Cricket Board]] |date=4 February 2026}}</ref>

== Background ==
In late 2025, [[Islamabad United]] became the first franchise to officially renew its partnership with the [[Pakistan Cricket Board|PCB]] for another decade. The [[2026 Pakistan Super League|2026]] season marked the league’s expansion to eight teams and introduced a player auction system with a team purse of PKR 450 million.<ref>{{cite news |last=Alam |first=Sher |date=4 February 2026 |title=Islamabad United Reveals Retention Amount for PSL Star Players |url=https://propakistani.pk/2026/02/04/islamabad-united-reveals-retention-amount-for-psl-star-players/ |work=ProPakistani}}</ref>

== Personnel ==
=== Coaching and Management Staff ===
In January 2026, the franchise announced the return of former player '''Luke Ronchi''' as the head coach, replacing Mike Hesson.<ref name="RonchiCoach">{{cite news |title=Former New Zealand cricketer Luke Ronchi named Islamabad United new head coach |url=https://a-sports.tv/luke-ronchi-appointed-islamabad-united-head-coach-psl-11 |work=A Sports |date=27 January 2026}}</ref>

* '''Head Coach:''' [[Luke Ronchi]]
* '''Assistant Coach:''' [[Jacob Oram]]
* '''Batting Coach:''' [[Ashley Wright (cricketer)|Ashley Wright]]
* '''Bowling Coach:''' [[Ian Butler (cricketer)|Ian Butler]]
* '''Owner:''' Ali Naqvi and Amna Naqvi (Leonine Global Sports)

=== Squad ===
Before the auction on 11 February 2026, Islamabad United retained [[Shadab Khan]], [[Devon Conway]] and [[Andries Gous]]from their '''2025''' squad. They also secured New Zealand's [[Devon Conway]] as their direct overseas signing for a reported PKR 6.3 crore (Rs. 63 million).<ref name="ConwayDirect">{{cite news |title=Karachi Kings, Islamabad United announce direct signings ahead of PSL 11 |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2590773/karachi-kings-islamabad-united-announce-direct-signings-ahead-of-psl-11 |work=[[The Express Tribune]] |date=4 February 2026}}</ref>
